title: How can two diagonals and their angle build a parallelogram?
description: The two diagonals are drawn first, crossing at their midpoints with the angle given. Joining the four ends in order gives the parallelogram, and the lengths are checked by adding the halves back.
teaching_notes: One idea: the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so each diagonal is split at its midpoint before the ends are joined. Watch for students who cross the diagonals at points that are not midpoints.

source: Figure it Out (parallelograms and rhombuses, question 2)
video_script.why: The child uses the fact that the diagonals bisect each other to construct a shape from its diagonals.
video_script.substitution: the book's question with diagonals 7 cm and 5 cm crossing at 140 degrees
video_script.anchor: two diagonals crossing at O at a 140 degree angle, with the four ends joined in order
video_script.payoff_line: Eigh B C D is the required parallelogram

final_answer.value: ABCD with AC = 7 cm, BD = 5 cm and 140°
final_answer.spoken: A B C D with diagonals of seven and five centimetres crossing at one hundred forty degrees

never_show: the diagonals crossing away from their midpoints
maths_rules: AC = 7 cm, so OA = OC = 7 / 2 = 3.5 cm
BD = 5 cm, so OB = OD = 5 / 2 = 2.5 cm
the angle between the diagonals at O is 140 degrees
the diagonals bisect each other at O, so ABCD is a parallelogram
video_script.design: One idea: the diagonals bisect each other, so each is split at its midpoint. The two diagonals are drawn first and the four ends are joined last.
